history.sg_progress: United Nations Secretariat entities continuously update delinquent equipment records, implement active measures to improve the utilization of their assets and assess their purchase plans to ensure better utilization of resources and to avoid unnecessary purchases. Entities have reviewed the data, analysed and documented the justification or reasons why each record or group of records were reported as idle and have taken corrective action where appropriate, with a view to avoiding future build-up of idle items. Slow-moving and obsolete property is initiated for write-off and disposal in line with the provisions of the delegation of authority. Special attention is paid to implementing measures for continuous enhancement of the quality of property records and ensuring that they correspond to the actual situation. The Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget has issued strategic guidance and a performance framework for property management for the financial year 2023 and provided further guidance on continuous enhancement of the utilization of property and the quality of records. The Office continues to monitor the performance of the action owners through the established performance framework for property management. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration, in coordination with the relevant department or office, analyse the reasons for assets remaining idle, actively use idle assets and retire unusable ones, and take more proactive measures to avoid further obsolescence in the future.
history.administration_response: The Administration has analysed the data on equipment in volume 1 entities reported as idle to determine the root causes of idle assets and reported its findings to the Board, which indicate that in addition to the justifiable need for maintaining equipment reserves at some entities for operational reasons, a large percentage of equipment items has been assigned an incorrect status in the Umoja system records. Some equipment items are not properly assigned upon issuance, nor are the equipment records updated by entities in a timely manner during and after the disposal process. The administration will further increase efforts to request entities to take immediate corrective actions, where appropriate, to address the incorrect equipment records. An extension to 30 September 2025 for the target date for implementation is requested.
history.board_assessment: Given that the average idle rate of computers held by United Nations Headquarters entities was 25 per cent in Umoja as of 31 March 2024, the Board consider this recommendation to be under implementation.
